records.authority: OpenAI is authoritative for its model release, plan and product availability statements, API price schedule, and its own benchmark and evaluation claims.
passages: OpenAI presents Sol and Luna as GPT-6 family models positioned for lower cost and faster work than Astra.
Its posted API prices are $2 input and $10 output per million tokens for GPT-6 Sol, and $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for GPT-6 Luna.
It says both models are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users, rolling out gradually.
It says they are not yet available in Chat.
It reports benchmark results and factuality improvements using OpenAI-described evaluation conditions.
records.limitation: All performance, factuality, comparison, cost-efficiency, and rollout claims are OpenAI claims. The stated availability is gradual and differs by product surface; no ordinary-Chat access can be inferred. Evaluation results do not establish typical-use performance.

records.authority: OpenAI controls its release, availability, plan, rollout and API-price statements.
passages: OpenAI lists GPT-6 Sol and Luna API pricing per million tokens.
OpenAI says the models are in ChatGPT Work and Codex, separate from Chat; plan and workspace settings affect available choices.
OpenAI says rollout is gradual and not a proof of one account’s available model picker.
records.limitation: Fresh official pages were inspected September 26. Provider claims remain attributed; account-specific access, cost, and real-world performance are not established.
